Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second essay! The two umpires have made their way out to the middle as have the England players. It will be Brandon King and Johnson Charles to open the innings for the West Indies. Reece Topley will start with the new ball for England. Off we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, West Indies will be the happier of the two sides at the halfway mark. Rovman Powell will be confident enough that his side can gun down this total on what is a tricky surface. As for England, the pitch isn't the easiest to bat on and they have the resources to make a match out of this. Can the English bowlers rise to the challenge? Join us in a bit to find out.

The man of the moment for West Indies, Gudakesh Motie is in for a chat. He says that he is very happy with his performance. Mentions that he bowled well and it was a really good day for him as he bowled in the correct line and correct length. Also says that The pitch is in favour of the bowlers as it was all about pitching in the right areas. Ends by praising Akeal Hosein as he is a very experienced bowler and he is trying to learn things from him.

As far as England are concerned, it was a real struggle for them. They kept losing wickets at untimely intervals which meant that they could not gather momentum at any stage of their batting effort. England's opening pair of Jos Buttler and Phil Salt made their intentions clear right from ball one. However, Buttler perished early with Will Jacks following suit. Phil Salt carried on but eventually got out to a peach of a delivery and Brook's departure put England firmly on the back foot. Moeen Ali joined hands with Liam Livingstone and began to counter-attack to steady the ship. Neither Ali nor Livingstone were able to convert their start and the incoming batters found it extremely difficult to hit the big shots.

England have been bowled out for 132! West Indies have risen to the occasion and have produced a dominant bowling performance to roll England over inside 20 overs! After opting to bowl first, West Indies showed that they were up for the challenge and started better than they did in the last two games. Andre Russell set the tone with an early wicket before Akeal Hosein struck in his second over. Gudakesh Motie did not have the best of outings in the last game but stepped up in this game to remove Phil Salt and Harry Brook in quick succession. West Indies kept chipping away with wickets at regular intervals between overs 10 and 20 and never allowed England to gain any momentum. Thanks to Andre Russell and Jason Holder, they were able to finish strongly with the ball. Gudakesh Motie registered his career-best figures of 3 for 24 from his four overs while Akeal Hosein, Andre Russell and Jason Holder chipped in with two wickets each.

OUT! CAUGHT! England are bundled out for 132 inside their 20 overs. Short of a length delivery angling across the batter. Curran stays deep in the crease and slaps it toward the long off region. He gets it from the toe end of the bat as Sherfane Rutherford runs around at the boundary and makes no mistake. Top effort from the Men in Maroon to restrict the World Champions to under 140. A wonderful outing with the ball for West Indies.

OUT! TAKEN! Jason Holder strikes in his first over! Jos Buttler tries to be inventive but it does not come off for the England skipper! Jason Holder serves it full, on the off-stump line, Jos Buttler shuffles across to scoop it up and over short fine leg. The delivery is a bit too full for him to get underneath and ends up scooping it straight into the bread basket of Oshane Thomas at short fine leg. Jason Holder leaps in the air in delight as do the WIndies fans!

Sherfane Rutherford dives to his left but fails to prevent the boundary. He lands awkwardly on his right hand and looks in some pain.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness now. West Indies are in a hudddle near the boundary before they spread their way onto the outfield. Phil Salt and Jos Buttler make their way out on the park for England while Andre Russell will start the proceedings with the ball for West Indies. Let's get rolling...

Jos Buttler, the England skipper, says that they were looking to chase but adds that the last game went well for them after batting first and he hopes to replicate that. Shares that a lot of sixes have been hit in the series and adds that it’s good to play the decider. Ends by saying that the boys are confident and looking forward to the match and informs that they are going with an unchanged team.

The captain of the West Indies, Rovman Powell says that they will bowl first. Adds that the wicket looks pretty good, and hopefully they can restrict the English batters. Mentions that it was a disappointing display in the previous match. Shares that they are doing their best to minimise the boundary count. Informs that Johnson Charles comes in for Kyle Mayers and Matthew Forde makes way for Oshane Thomas.
England (Unchanged Playing XI) - Phil Salt (WK), Jos Buttler (C), Will Jacks, Liam Livingstone, Harry Brook, Moeen Ali, Sam Curran, Chris Woakes, Rehan Ahmed, Adil Rashid, Reece Topley.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Johnson Charles (In place of Kyle Mayers), Shai Hope, Nicholas Pooran (WK), Sherfane Rutherford, Rovman Powell (C), Gudakesh Motie, Andre Russell, Jason Holder, Akeal Hosein, Oshane Thomas (In place of Matthew Forde).
TOSS - West Indies have won the coin toss and Rovman Powell has opted to BOWL first.

On the other hand, the West Indies will have to re-strategize their plans, as whatever they had planned for England in the first two matches of the series has not worked since the last two. The bowling unit of the Windies had no answers to the assault from the England batters. Akeal Hosein, Jason Holder, and Andre Russell managed to take a wicket each, but it was not enough to prevent the damage. As a result, their batters had to go for the big shots but failed to execute them properly. Andre Russell, Nicholas Pooran, and Sherfane Rutherford were the only bright spots for them with the bat. Rovman Powell's men will have to put the two losses behind them and start afresh in the series decider. Will England continue with their momentum in the series? Or will the Windies fight back? Let's find out. Toss and team news in a bit. Stay tuned!

England have made an exceptional comeback in this five-match T20I series. They lost the first two matches of the series, but they were able to step up for a fightback. In the last match, Phil Salt led the way with an impressive knock of 119 off just 57 deliveries. Jos Buttler and Liam Livingstone did their part too, before Reece Topley, Sam Curran, and Rehan Ahmed combined to seal the win for England. The only worrying aspect of the match was that the English bowlers were expensive and leaked a lot of boundaries. Although they managed to take the wickets at crucial stages, they will have to be economical in this game.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the 5th and final match of this T20I series between the West Indies and England at the Brian Lara Stadium in Tarouba. The series is currently poised at 2-2, and the stage is set for a series decider as the West Indies take on the visiting England side for one final time this year.
... MATCH DAY ...

We are now down to the fifth and final game of the T20I series between the West Indies and England at the Brian Lara Stadium in Trinidad. After the West Indies took the first two games convincingly and went 2-0 up in the series, England roared back in the next two matches to draw level. As a result, the visitors have momentum with them heading into the fifth T20I, whereas the hosts have tapered off a bit and will have to bring their A-game to clinch the series. In the fourth T20I at Trinidad, Phil Salt stood out with another scintillating hundred and responded in his own way after being overlooked at the Indian T20 League auction. Jos Buttler and Liam Livingstone chipped in as well to help England post 267, their highest total in the format. In reply, the West Indies started well and kept up with the required run rate but lost wickets at regular intervals, which meant that the game escaped them. Rovman Powell will be worried that his bowlers have allowed England to score over 200 in the last two games. Even though Akeal Hosein may not have picked wickets, he has done a decent job of keeping things quiet. Jason Holder, Gudakesh Motie, and Andre Russell were pretty expensive, and if the West Indies are to get the desired result, this trio will have to pull their socks up. As far as their batting goes, many batters have gotten starts but have not been able to convert them into big scores like Phil Salt has done for England. Nicholas Pooran, Rovman Powell, and Brandon King have done the heavy lifting, whereas Shai Hope and Kyle Mayers have struggled in the series, which has not helped the team's cause. On the other hand, England looked down and out after losing the first two T20Is, but they have clicked collectively as a unit to take the series to a decider. Phil Salt has led England's fightback in the series with back-to-back hundreds, while the likes of Jos Buttler, Liam Livingstone, and Harry Brook have done well to bat around him. The newly crowned number one ranked T20I bowler, Adil Rashid, has weaved his magic, and he has found good support from fellow leggie Rehan Ahmed. Their pace department, comprising Chris Woakes, Reece Topley, and Tymal Mills, has been gone for runs, which might be a headache for Jos Buttler in the series finale. The stage is set for a grandstand finish, and it promises to be a mouthwatering prospect. Who are you backing to emerge victorious?
